parallel.requirements: Recognized the cleanroom requirement, the prohibition on source lookup and binary analysis, and the need to match the provided age CLI by black-box execution and bundled docs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while delegating eight behavior-probing areas to a workflow and planning a critic phase to reconcile spec gaps.
parallel.implementation: The parent created a Go module, compile.sh, internal packages, SHA-3/SHAKE, ChaCha20-Poly1305 tests, and KDF code, but never reached a complete CLI implementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact contained partial Go package files and compile.sh, plus docs and the original executable, but no completed integrated replacement executable.
parallel.verification: The parent ran focused unit tests for SHA-3 and ChaCha20-Poly1305; child probes produced many behavioral observations, but the full project was not built or evaluated locally before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow result was null and killed, many children were interrupted, the final response was empty, and the official evaluator failed at compile time with 0/839 tests run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same cleanroom reverse-engineering task and restriction to executing the binary and reading bundled docs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as one actor with no workflow or subagents, combining documentation reading, probing, Python helper development, and exploratory validation locally.
serial.implementation: Built Python bech32 and age crypto prototypes in /tmp/w and probed CLI behaviors, but did not create the required source project in /workspace.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted tree contained only the original workspace files, docs, git metadata, and executable; there was no compile.sh or replacement implementation in the artifact.
serial.verification: Verified Python primitives and several black-box behaviors such as scrypt, armor, prompts, and wordlist sampling, but never ran a final replacement build or acceptance test.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with an empty final response and official compile_failed result, leaving the benchmark with no buildable submitted implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent understood that the target was an age CLI and that only execution and bundled docs were allowed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same cleanroom constraints and documented age behavior from the bundled files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference explains the outcome; both understood the high-level task and both failed later at delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior mapping into eight probe areas plus a critic while the parent retained implementation work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed probing and helper implementation in one continuous local trajectory with no delegated work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created a broad workflow dependency for behavior knowledge; serial avoided child ownership boundaries but also lacked enough time to finish implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs had exact spec-output paths and a common scratch protocol, and the critic was supposed to read all generated specs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all observations in one context and did not need cross-agent handoffs or child-return contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference was the parallel run's dependency on a workflow aggregate that never arrived, not a missing task requirement or interface contract in an individual brief.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel began a Go reimplementation in /workspace and wrote crypto package files with passing focused unit tests for some primitives.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented probing and crypto validation helpers under /tmp/w, not a submitted source tree under /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel got closer to a submitted codebase, while serial gathered useful behavioral knowledge but left the final artifact essentially unimplemented.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow was launched in the background and the state file shows result null and status killed before the parent could receive the aggregate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its work products stayed local to the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the intended child aggregate result at workflow termination, while serial had no such retrieval boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered a partial Go tree with internal packages and compile.sh but no finished executable integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation lists only existing docs, git metadata, license, README, and executable, with no submitted implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partial workspace integration but no complete build; serial did not move its helper code into the final submitted tree at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran package-level tests for crypto primitives but no final integrated acceptance test before the official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified behavioral probes and Python crypto experiments, but did not build or test a replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had exploratory verification only; neither closed the loop with a buildable final artifact, and the official evaluator did not reach behavioral tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent substantial budget in the workflow, including stalled retries, then the main process timed out and the workflow was killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed the full time budget, but without child work or workflow retries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's budget pressure was amplified by the broad child fan-out; serial's budget failure was ordinary single-agent scope overrun.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both modes completed official evaluation with compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 0/839 tests run. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel created a partial Go project but lost the broad workflow result to timeout, while serial stayed in one context and produced only local probes and Python helpers outside the submitted workspace.
parallel_contributors: Partial Go implementation existed in the submitted tree but stopped far short of a complete CLI.
The child workflow was killed with no aggregate result after broad fan-out and stalled retries.
serial_contributors: Serial never created a compile.sh or replacement implementation in the submitted workspace.
Serial spent the run on documentation, behavioral probing, and helper scripts under /tmp/w.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel chose a Go source-tree path; serial mostly used Python probes and did not assemble final code.
Both lacked a completed buildable executable, so the evaluator stopped at compile failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both_fail comparison; retained parallel pattern is adverse but does not explain an outcome split

Investigation and implementation overlapped after workflow launch; the parent did not wait for all probes before starting code.
The evidence points to collective fan-out and retries exhausting budget, not an auxiliary-work allocation starving a distinct critical path.
